brief: BULB DIVE: a real-time raymarched 3D fractal explorer in raw WebGL (no libraries). Default subject is the Mandelbulb (White-Nylander power-n formula in spherical coordinates, power 8), plus at least two more distance-estimated fractals (for example the Mandelbox and a Menger sponge or a quaternion Julia set) with correct distance estimators. Rendering: sphere tracing with the distance estimator, soft shadows, ambient occlusion from step count, orbit-trap colouring with selectable palettes, depth fog, gamma-correct output. Camera: drag to orbit, wheel/pinch to zoom toward the surface (zoom speed scales with the distance estimate so you can dive deep), double-click/tap to fly toward a point, plus an Autopilot mode that glides along the surface. Performance is critical: adaptive resolution (render to a smaller offscreen framebuffer while moving, then progressively refine to full resolution when still), cap devicePixelRatio, iteration and step budgets tied to a Quality setting. UI: fractal picker, power/parameter sliders with live morphing (power 2 to 16), palette picker, quality, Save view to localStorage (try/catch) and Reset. Show the formula being rendered as a small readout, plus live numbers: power, camera distance, ray steps, frame time. WebGL1 fallback if WebGL2 is missing; a clear message panel if there is no WebGL at all. The test harness renders WebGL in software (SwiftShader), so make the very first frame cheap enough to appear quickly and still look striking.
